subject: MiraTech pilot: proposed evaluation plan, timeline, and model shortlist
messages:
From: Alex Grant <alex.grant@miratech.ai>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Cc: Sarah Liu <sarah.liu@miratech.ai>
Date: Mon, 11 Jun 2028 15:12:03 -0700
Subject: Quick follow-up: pilot goals & data scope

Thanks again for the demo today — appreciate the walk-through. A quick recap and a few clarifying Qs so we can align on a trial that proves value for our clinical summarization use case.

High-level goals (what success looks like):
- Reduce clinician summary editing time by >=40% on average for outpatient notes.
- Preserve key clinical facts (meds, allergies, plan) with >95% recall in the extracted summary.
- Support English + Spanish + French (initial dataset covers these).

Data & testing constraints:
- We can provide 1,200 de-identified notes (split across locales) plus a 200-note holdout set.
- Latency target for interactive review is ~ P50 <300ms, P95 <900ms.

Questions we had:
1) Which open models would you recommend for this workload with a focus on accuracy + multilingual support?
2) What fallback model would you put in the rotation if capacity/latency looks tight?
3) What minimal sandbox timeline do you recommend to produce an objective evaluation?

Next steps from our side: provide the data extract and a sample acceptance rubric by EOD Friday. Can Redwood draft a proposed pilot hypothesis, evaluation metrics, and a timeline (we'd like something we can sign off on quickly so procurement can greenlight dev effort).

Thanks — looking forward to the plan.

Alex
Alex Grant
Head of Product
MiraTech Health

--
Attachment: sample_prompts.xlsx (spreadsheet of 30 example notes)

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Alex Grant <alex.grant@miratech.ai>
Cc: Sarah Liu <sarah.liu@miratech.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 12 Jun 2028 09:07:18 -0700
Subject: RE: Quick follow-up: pilot goals & data scope

Alex — thanks for the clear summary and the sample prompts. I outlined a compact pilot plan below that aims to give you objective comparisons across accuracy, latency, and cost within a 3-week sandbox. Please review and tell us where you'd like more detail.

Proposed pilot in brief (3-week sandbox):
- Week 0 (prep): Redwood ingests de-id dataset, ingest sanity checks, and creates deterministic prompt templates. (Owner: Aditya)
- Week 1 (sandbox runs): Run batch evaluations across 3 candidate models on the 1,200-note set plus a 200-note holdout. Collect latency profiles and token cost estimates. (Owner: Aditya + Soojin)
- Week 2 (human review): Marissa will coordinate clinical SME review on 200 holdout notes to measure recall/precision on key fields and an overall clinician acceptance score. Deliverable: evaluation report + ranked model shortlist. (Owner: Marissa)

Candidate model shortlist (initial):
- Mistral-Instruct-v1 (strong instruction-following, good multilingual priors)
- Llama-2-13b-chat (4-bit quantized; good balance of cost/accuracy)
- RedWood-Open-7B-Med (lighter, faster fallback for heavy load — lower cost, lower accuracy)

Fallback strategy:
- Primary: Mistral-Instruct for accuracy-sensitive flows (when latency OK).
- Fallback: RedWood-Open-7B-Med automatically for short bursts or during degraded capacity; route by policy so the UI signals which summaries used fallback.

Evaluation metrics & acceptance thresholds (draft):
- Clinical fact recall (meds, allergies, plan) >= 95% recall on holdout (measured by blind SME comparison)
- Clinician edit-time reduction >= 35% (measured via timed edit task)
- Summary quality score >= 4.0/5 average from SME review
- Latency: P50 < 350ms and P95 < 900ms for the chosen model in the dedicated sandbox environment

Logistics & timeline:
- Draft pilot SOW delivered by Redwood 6/13
- Data handoff by MiraTech 6/14
- Sandbox runs start 6/17; final report 7/05

Open items / asks for you:
- Confirm locales to include (we assumed EN, ES, FR)
- Any regulatory constraints on where data can be processed (US-only vs EU allowed)
- Who on your side will be the clinical SME for the review?

I'll attach a one-page pilot scope and a sample rubric. If these targets look reasonable, I can loop in Procurement/Legal for a short SOW.

Thanks,
Soojin
Soojin Lee
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
soojin_lee@redwood.com

--
Attachments: miratech_pilot_scope_v1.pdf, pilot_sample_prompts.xlsx

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Grant <alex.grant@miratech.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 13 Jun 2028 11:33:47 -0700
Subject: RE: Quick follow-up: pilot goals & data scope

Thanks — copying the pilot plan into a few acceptance-focused bullets. A couple of short edits to thresholds that will make the report more actionable for your stakeholders.

On Tue, Jun 12, 2028 at 9:07 AM Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com> wrote:
> Alex — thanks for the clear summary and the sample prompts. I outlined a compact pilot plan below that aims to give you objective comparisons across accuracy, latency, and cost within a 3-week sandbox. Please review and tell us where you'd like more detail.

Acceptance parity (suggested firm thresholds):
- Clinical fact recall >= 95% over holdout set (binary pass/fail per fact type)
- False positive rate on extracted problems/meds < 3% (clinically important)
- Average clinician acceptability >= 4.2/5 (raises bar for production readiness)
- Latency SLO: P50 < 300ms, P95 < 800ms when tested on a Dedicated small pool (simulating prod)
- Cost: baseline cost estimate per 1k tokens and a projected monthly run-rate at 100k notes/day (we'll provide the calc in the report)

Operational notes:
- We should include a simple fallback UX flag so clinicians know if a summary was generated by the fallback model. That reduces trust friction during evaluation.
- Aditya, can you confirm whether we can spin a Dedicated small pool for the sandbox dates (6/17–7/05) and what quotas would be needed?

I'll own the SME coordination and the rubric; Soojin and Aditya, happy to sync briefly to finalize the rubric before we run the human reviews.

Marissa
Marissa Cole
Customer Success Lead | Redwood Inference
